snippet.title: Countdown To Daughter from Hell: Gracie Abrams in conversation w/ Olivia Rodrigo
snippet.description:
For Gracie Abrams, growing up means learning to look inwards instead of pointing fingers. It means understanding that we’ve been both the antagonist and the protagonist in conflict. Growing up is recognizing that most honest songs come from the hardest-won perspective.

Gracie sits down with her friend and fellow songwriter Olivia Rodrigo to talk about her new album: a record two years in the making, built on tour buses, and finished in studios in London and New York. Gracie describes Daughter from Hell as more existential than diaristic. It’s less about relitigating the past, but rather understanding it with empathy and maturity. 

Together, the two songwriters discuss Gracie's creative evolution, swap stories from the road, and dissect the making and meaning behind tracks like “Daughter from Hell” and “Humming.”
Between Olivia's genuine curiosity and Gracie's reflective nature, what unfolds is less an interview than a conversation between two artists who've watched each other grow. This is what it looks like when two of their generation's most gifted songwriters finally get a moment to just sit and talk.

snippet.title: Trueno & Leandro Paredes Discuss TURR4ZO | Watch Countdown To on Spotify
snippet.description:
“I need to experience things so I can write later. I need to nurture myself to learn so that it inspires me at some point… what I experience is more important than what I write, because if I don’t experience anything, I can’t write anything,” says Trueno, who returns with TURR4ZO, a project shaped through lived experience and a deeper connection to his roots.

Shot at El Obrero, a historic dining spot in La Boca, the neighborhood where he was born and raised. Trueno sits down with Argentine professional footballer Leandro Paredes to reflect on the making of the album, unpacking its direction, his evolution, and the responsibility that comes with representing Argentina on a global stage. Drawing parallels between music and sport, the conversation centers on cultural impact and what it means to be a voice for a new generation.

Breaking down the creative process, he explains how TURR4ZO leans into classic Argentinian and Uruguayan influences and samples, a shift from the U.S. hip hop influences that defined his earlier work. He also speaks on the significance of the number 4, framing it as a defining element of the project and the album he connects with the most.

Presave TUR4ZZO out on Spotify: https://open.spotify.com/prerelease/3WZjBRPv6UO3qamlkqrPoE?si=991de0da0d18414e

Listen to Trueno on Spotify: https://open.spotify.com/artist/1mcTU81TzQhprhouKaTkpq?si=-8eN4SYtT2mhxnpnqPpPOg

“Necesito vivir cosas para poder después escribir necesito nutrí y conocer para que eso me inspire en cierto punto….lo que vivo es más importante que lo que escribo por que si no vivo nada no puedo escribir nada”, dice Trueno, quien regresa con TURR4ZO, un proyecto construido desde la experiencia y una conexión más profunda con sus raíces.

Filmado en El Obrero, un bodegón histórico en La Boca, el barrio donde nació y creció, Trueno se sienta con el futbolista argentino Leandro Paredes para reflexionar sobre la creación del álbum, hablando sobre su dirección, su evolución y la responsabilidad de representar a Argentina a nivel global. Haciendo paralelos entre la música y el deporte, la conversación se centra en el impacto cultural y en lo que significa ser una voz para una nueva generación.

Al hablar del proceso creativo, explica cómo TURR4ZO se apoya en influencias y samples clásicos argentinos y uruguayos, marcando un cambio versus las influencias del hip hop de Estados Unidos que definieron sus proyectos anteriores. También habla sobre el significado del número 4, viéndolo como un elemento clave del álbum y el proyecto con el que más se identifica.

snippet.title: All Access Pass: Young Thug's Homecoming Show | Spotify
snippet.description:
Young Thug returns to Atlanta for his Hometown Hero Benefit Concert at State Farm Arena, and we went All Access for one of the most important nights in Atlanta rap history. In this behind-the-scenes look at his homecoming show, we follow the full journey from arrival at State Farm Arena to post-show backstage moments. Friends, family, and collaborators including T.I., Quavo, Ty Dolla $ign, Lil Gotit, and more pull up to show love, while Thug’s attorney Brian Steel and his sister HiDoraah share the moment.

You’ll also hear from his engineer Bainzz on how Thug found his sound, Taurus on Thug’s first show back in Atlanta, and Young Thug himself reflecting on what this night meant and what he’s working on next. The night wraps with post-show celebrations and a special appearance from Thug’s fiancée, Mariah the Scientist, showing off her engagement ring. This is Young Thug: All Access Pass, live from Atlanta.

snippet.title: UK R&B Roundtable on Legacy, Labels, and Belonging | Spotify Conversations
snippet.description:
DJ Ace leads a powerful roundtable with UK R&B powerhouses Craig David, Mahalia, and Tiana Major9 in an honest conversation about the state of R&B in the UK and the experiences shaping their artistry. From their earliest musical memories to navigating international success and industry expectations, they unpack what it means to belong in a space that hasn't always embraced them.

They reflect on church roots, British music culture, and the influence of American R&B, while also calling out industry challenges around colorism, visibility, and recognition. This episode is a vital reminder of the importance of representation, storytelling, and creating space for future generations of UK R&B talent.

snippet.title: Rauw Alejandro w/ Wisin and Ñengo Flow | Spotify Countdown To Cosa Nuestra: Capítulo 0
snippet.description:
“Every time I drop an album I’m like, ‘This is my best album.’ It’s because you keep leveling up,” says Puerto Rican superstar Rauw Alejandro, who returns with Cosa Nuestra Capítulo 0, a bold new record that puts the Caribbean sounds forward.

Shot at El Refugio in Río Piedras, Rauw sits down with Puerto Rican legends Wisin and Ñengo Flow to reflect on the making of the album, unpacking its inspiration, his evolution as an artist, and the importance of identity. Breaking down the prequel concept, he explains how Cosa Nuestra centered on the story and sounds inspired by Puerto Rican migration to New York. With Cosa Nuestra Capítulo 0, the focus shifts to a project that pays homage to Caribbean culture at its core, anchored in the Caribbean connection.

A conversation between three generations of Latin music, shared between laughs and a game of pool, offers a glimpse into how Rauw Alejandro has matured as an artist and how legends such as Wisin and Ñengo Flow see him as an important force for today’s generation.

snippet.title: Meet Thakzin Originator of 3 Step Afro House | Spotify RADAR Africa
snippet.description:
Born to a South African and Mozambican family, Thakzin’s journey began in Ivory Park, Johannesburg, where early jazz and kwaito influences, plus a deep respect for traditional percussion, shaped his signature sound. 

Get to know the South African Afro House DJ and producer as he shares how music resonates with him on a deeper, spiritual level. Thakzin’s sound is rooted in African spirituality and healing, inspired by the rhythmic power of traditional drums. 

Discover how his sound moved across borders to be enjoyed on a global stage, and how he laid the foundation for the 3 Step sub-genre of music.

snippet.title: Artists describe Afrobeats in their own words - Spotify
snippet.description:
Culture in Motion follows Afrobeats as it travels from Lagos to Bogotá, tracing a generation remixing heritage into tomorrow. 

Through intimate portraits of rising Nigerian voices and Colombian artists newly fluent in Afrobeats, the film charts a living conversation across the Atlantic, where drum patterns, pidgin hooks, and barrio cadences meet. It's culture on the move: West African style, slang, and spirituality finding new homes without losing its roots. In studios and street parties, this new wave taps a shared Afro-diasporic history to make something unapologetically global, unmistakably local, and irresistibly danceable, and celebrates the kinship between Africa and Latin America.

snippet.title: Countdown To Am I The Drama?: Cardi B in conversation w/ Kelly Rowland | Spotify
snippet.description:
In Cardi B’s world, owning your truth, speaking without hesitation, and refusing to shrink yourself when something isn’t right is worth causing a bit of drama.

The iconic rapper returns with her long-awaited second studio album, “AM I THE DRAMA?” It’s a body of work that’s unapologetic, decadent and deeply intentional – reflecting exactly where Cardi stands seven years after her debut.

In conversation with her friend, fellow icon and mom-confidante Kelly Rowland, Cardi opens up about love, fame, artistry and the power of authenticity. The two celebrate their bond, unpack the creative process and get candid about navigating emotion under the spotlight.

Between Cardi’s signature unfiltered moments and Kelly’s warm and inquisitive nature, we get a look into the making of this era and a taste of everything fans can expect from one of music’s most commanding voices.
